choosing_cycle.question: Which engine cycle should I use?
choosing_cycle.quick_check: Pressure-fed (tiny, short duration) → Gas generator (medium bipropellant) → Tap-off (small-medium) → Expander (LOX/LH2) → Staged combustion (large LOX engines). Pump discharge ~k·Pc varies by cycle; turbine PR sets stress.

injector_pressure_drop.question: What injector pressure drop should I design for?
injector_pressure_drop.quick_check: Normal bipropellant: 15–20 % of Pc (balance feed-system weight vs. stability/atomization). Staged combustion & small thrusters: 0.3–0.5 for injector stiffness. Low Δp minimizes pump power; high Δp enhances combustion stability.

injector_type.question: What injector type is best?
injector_type.quick_check: Triplet (most common, eliminates β-vs-MR drift) → Quintuplet (higher perf) → Coaxial hollow-post (LOX/GH2, not for storable bipropellants). For pressure-fed monopropellants or low-Pc: simple showerhead acceptable. Highest element count → smallest droplets → best vaporization.

cooling_method.question: How should I cool the chamber and nozzle?
cooling_method.quick_check: Regenerative (medium–large bipropellant, high Pc). Film/transpiration (high local flux). Radiation (low flux, monopropellant, nozzle extensions ε > ~6–10). Ablative (low Pc < 250 psi, fuel-rich exhaust required; avoid 4–15 % duty pulsing). Higher Pc → higher heat flux → sets material/cooling limit.
cooling_method.heat_flux_note: Only 0.5–5 % of total energy reaches walls. Peak at throat. Radiation 5–35 % of transferred heat.

regenerative_coolant_choice.question: What coolant should I use for regenerative cooling?
regenerative_coolant_choice.quick_check: LOX/RP-1: ΔT limit ~120 K (coking), Isp credit 0.1–1.5 %. LOX/LH2: ΔT limit ~500 K, higher credit. Real GH2/LOX needed ~7.5 % coolant flow by mass (304 SS, 2000 °R limit). Coolant-side ΔT is the constraint; regen absorbs heat and augments exhaust velocity.

c_star_efficiency.question: What c* efficiency should I assume for this propellant pair?
c_star_efficiency.quick_check: Use real-engine calibrations from validate.py: LOX/RP-1 0.955, LOX/LH2 0.94, N2O4/MMH 0.90, Aerozine/NTO 0.9435, Hydrazine 0.80. Literature band 0.96–0.99 for good chambers. Reverse-solve new pairs against real engines in Engine_Configs/.
c_star_efficiency.process: Spot-check rule: find real engine with same propellant → solve for η_c* → add to validate.py SPOT_CHECKS

chamber_lstar.question: What L* (chamber length) should I use?
chamber_lstar.quick_check: Typical L* 15–120 (corresponds to stay time 0.001–0.040 s). C* rises asymptotically with L*; beyond ~20–40, more L* only adds mass/cooled area. Design for 'essentially complete combustion' plateau; overly long chambers add waste mass.

nozzle_bell_contour.question: Should I use a conical or bell nozzle?
nozzle_bell_contour.quick_check: Bell nozzles gain 8–15 % of Isp over conical (shorter, lighter, better thrust coefficient). Trade-off: more complex to machine/analyze. Modern engines use bell (Rao-parabolic or similar). Conical still used for simplicity/rapid-dev (e.g., small thrusters).
nozzle_bell_contour.reference_table: Sutton Fig 3-14 (Rao θn/θe vs ε table, digitized in design.py)

radiation_cooling_transition.question: At what nozzle expansion ratio can I switch to radiation cooling?
radiation_cooling_transition.quick_check: Radiation cooling becomes viable beyond ε ~6–10 (nozzle exit area ratio). Low heat flux at high ε allows cheaper/simpler refractory materials (Mo-0.5Ti, 90Ta-10W). Pc must be < ~250 psi. Material must be refractory (good to 3500 °R).
radiation_cooling_transition.design_constant: cooling.py default: cooling_transition_eps 6.0 (conservative end of range)

materials_high_pressure.question: What materials work at high chamber pressure and heat flux?
materials_high_pressure.quick_check: Hot-gas side: Inconel 625, stainless 304/347 (thin-wall regen), Rene 41 (> 2000 psi). Turbine rotor (> 1000 K inlet): directional-solidified Ni-base superalloys. Pump housing/impeller: 7075-T73 aluminum or stainless 17-4PH. Avoid high-strength steel in LH2 (hydrogen embrittlement).

chamber_pressure_limit.question: What's the practical upper limit on chamber pressure?
chamber_pressure_limit.quick_check: Higher Pc → higher heat flux → sets material/cooling limit. Achievable Pc depends on cooling method and material choice. Regeneratively cooled bipropellants: 3000–5000 psia typical (F-1 ~2700, RS-25 ~3250, RD-180 ~3450). Pressure-fed: limited by tank pressure (< 500 psia typical).

gas_generator_fuel_ratio.question: What fuel-rich mixture ratio should my gas generator use?
gas_generator_fuel_ratio.quick_check: GG mixture ratio 0.2–1.0 (fuel-rich). Higher MR = lower temperature (reduces hot-streak damage). UMR (uniform) gives consistent T everywhere; hot-core (lean center + rich annulus) gains c* but requires precise injector design. Both approaches used in real engines.

turbine_efficiency.question: What turbine efficiency can I assume?
turbine_efficiency.quick_check: Real GG & staged-combustion turbines: 46–70 %, most 55–66 % [SP-8107 Table III]. design.py uses GG_ETA_TURBINE = 0.62 (mid-band, conservative). Real RD-0110 & RD-0124 both ~55–66 % range.

spot_check_new_design.question: How do I validate a new engine design?
spot_check_new_design.quick_check: (1) Reverse-solve c* efficiency against a real engine with the same propellant + Pc + MR. (2) Cross-check Isp predicted vs real engine (should be within 1–2 %). (3) Check heat flux vs material thermal limits. (4) Check turbopump specific power vs real turbopumps (50 000–150 000 W/kg). (5) Run full validate.py suite to catch coefficient/constant inconsistencies.
spot_check_new_design.process: Add new propellant to SPOT_CHECKS in physics/validate.py; run full suite

heat_flux_ranges.low: < 0.3 kW/cm² (gas gen, nozzle extension, small thruster)
heat_flux_ranges.peak_location: Always at nozzle throat; lowest near exit

chamber_lstar_by_propellant.asymptote: Performance plateaus; excess L* adds waste mass

discharge_coefficient_Cd.rule: Well-rounded entrance + smooth bore → high Cd → lower ΔP

combustion_stay_time.calculation: ts = Vc / (ṁ·V̄) where V̄ is mean specific volume

cooling_method_by_heat_flux.low_flux: Radiation (ε > 6–10) or ablative (fuel-rich exhaust, Pc < 250 psi)
